---
title: "🐟 Species and countries"
description: >
  species_country(), country_species() and country_analysis(): who catches a species,
  what a country catches in an area, and a country's catch in all FAO areas.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_setup.R")
FAO34 <- suppressMessages(fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Eastern Central", plot = FALSE))
```

```{r data-source, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
data_source()
```

These functions take the fishing area data of `fishing_area_data()` (here area 34) and look at
one species or one country. `country_analysis()` looks at a country in all FAO areas.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
FAO34 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Eastern Central")
```

## 1️⃣ `species_country()`: who catches a species

Names must match the FAO species names exactly; the main species of an area are a good start:

```{r}
top <- aggregate(Production ~ ASFIS.species..Name., data = FAO34$area_data, FUN = sum)
head(top[order(-top$Production), "ASFIS.species..Name."], 10)
```

```{r, figures = TRUE}
sardine <- species_country(FAO34$area_data, species_name = "European pilchard(=Sardine)")
```

In the file names, `<species>` is the species name with spaces and punctuation replaced by `_`
(e.g. `European_pilchard__Sardine_`):

| File | Chart |
|---|---|
| `<species>_country_map.png` | Catch of the species by country over all years, on a world map |
| `species/<species>_country_ranked_total.png` | Total catch and share of the selected countries (by default the ten main ones) |
| `species/<species>_country_ranked.png` | Their catch over time |
| `species/<species>_country_ranked_wrap.png` | One panel per country, with its share, a linear trend and the breakpoints of its mean catch (with `timeseries_analysis = FALSE`, a smooth curve) |
| `species/<species>_country_pie_selected.png` | Shares of the main countries in each decade and in each year of the current decade (up to four countries, the others are grouped) |

The table `tables/<species>_country_ranked_table.csv` has the average catch per decade, the catch
in the last five years and the share of each country in the last year:

```{r}
table <- read.csv("tables/European_pilchard__Sardine__country_ranked_table.csv",
                  fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM", check.names = FALSE)
show_table(table, n = 10, digits = 0)
```

With `timeseries_analysis = TRUE` the function returns a list of two data frames: the catch of
the selected countries by year (`sardine[[1]]`) and their breakpoints (`sardine[[2]]`: start
year, end year and mean catch of each period); with `timeseries_analysis = FALSE`, only the
first.

### Options

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `area_data` | Catch data of an area: `fishing_area_data()$area_data` or any subset of `load_fao_data()` | |
| `species_name` | FAO species name (ASFIS English name, as in the data) | |
| `rank_range` | Ranks of the countries shown, by total catch of the species over all years | `c(1, 10)` |
| `plot` | Save the charts | `TRUE` |
| `table` | Save the table in `tables/` | `TRUE` |
| `timeseries_analysis` | `TRUE`: panel chart with linear trend and breakpoints; `FALSE`: panel chart with a smooth (loess) curve | `TRUE` |
| `h_value` | Minimum length of a period between breakpoints: a fraction of the series or a number of years | `0.15` |
| `polygon_color` | Colour of the country borders on the map | `"grey90"` |
| `fill_scale` | Palette of the map, any choice of `map_palette` in `fao_settings()` | `NULL`: `map_palette` of `fao_settings()` (`"deep-orange"`) |
| `axis_title_face` | Font face of the axis titles of the map | `"bold"` |
| `axis_title_size_map` | Size of the axis titles of the map | `14` |
| `axis_text_size_map` | Size of the axis labels of the map | `12` |
| `legend_text_size_map` | Size of the legend text of the map | `12` |
| `axis_text_size`, `axis_title_size` | Size of the axis labels and titles of the other charts | `10`, `12` |
| `strip_text_size`, `strip_text_face` | Size and font face of the panel titles | `12`, `"bold"` |
| `ZH` | Older way of asking for Chinese: `TRUE` is `lang = "zh"` | `FALSE` |
| `lang` | Language of the chart text and names: `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | `NULL`: `"zh"` if `ZH = TRUE`, else the language of `fao_settings()` |
| `pptx` | Also save the charts as editable PowerPoint files | `FALSE`, or `pptx` of `fao_settings()` |

::: callout-note
In the current version the ranking, time series, panel and pie charts of `species_country()` use
fixed text sizes: `axis_text_size`, `axis_title_size`, `strip_text_size` and `strip_text_face`
are accepted but do not change them. The map arguments do.
:::

Tuna series are short in some countries; a larger `h_value` gives clearer breakpoints:

```{r, figures = "wrap"}
species_country(FAO34$area_data, species_name = "Skipjack tuna", h_value = 5, lang = "zh")
```

## 2️⃣ `country_species()`: what a country catches in the area

```{r, figures = TRUE}
morocco <- country_species(FAO34$area_data, country_name = "Morocco")
```

In the file names, `<country>` is the country name with spaces and punctuation replaced by `_`:

| File | Chart |
|---|---|
| `country/<country>_species_ranked_total.png` | Total catch and share of the country's selected species (by default the ten main ones) |
| `country/<country>_species_ranked.png` | Their catch over time |
| `country/<country>_species_ranked_wrap.png` | One panel per species, with share, trend and breakpoints |
| `country/<country>_species_pie_selected.png` | Species shares in each decade and in each year of the current decade |
| `tables/<country>_country_ranked_table.csv` | Average catch per decade, catch in the last five years and share in the last year of each species |

It returns the catch of the selected species by year.

`time_analysis_text_displacement` moves the share labels in the panel chart (years after the first
year with catch), useful when they overlap the lines:

```{r, figures = "wrap"}
country_species(FAO34$area_data, country_name = "Spain", h_value = 5,
                time_analysis_text_displacement = 6, lang = "both")
```

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `area_data` | Catch data of an area: `fishing_area_data()$area_data` or any subset of `load_fao_data()` | |
| `country_name` | FAO country name, as in the data | |
| `rank_range` | Ranks of the species shown, by the country's total catch over all years | `c(1, 10)` |
| `plot` | Save the charts | `TRUE` |
| `table` | Save the table in `tables/` | `TRUE` |
| `timeseries_analysis` | `TRUE`: panel chart with linear trend and breakpoints; `FALSE`: panel chart with a smooth (loess) curve | `TRUE` |
| `time_analysis_text_displacement` | Position of the share labels in the panel chart: number of years after the first year with catch | `10` |
| `h_value` | Minimum length of a period between breakpoints: a fraction of the series or a number of years | `0.15` |
| `ZH` | Older way of asking for Chinese: `TRUE` is `lang = "zh"` | `FALSE` |
| `lang` | Language of the chart text and names: `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | `NULL`: `"zh"` if `ZH = TRUE`, else the language of `fao_settings()` |
| `pptx` | Also save the charts as editable PowerPoint files | `FALSE`, or `pptx` of `fao_settings()` |

## 3️⃣ `country_analysis()`: a country in all FAO areas

`country_analysis()` uses the catch of a country in **all** FAO areas, so it takes the country name
only:

```{r, figures = TRUE}
morocco_global <- country_analysis(country_name = "Morocco")
```

Besides the species charts (as in `country_species()`, file names `<country>analysis_...`), it
saves:

| File | Chart |
|---|---|
| `country/<country>fishing_area_map.png` | The country's total catch in each FAO area, on a map of the FAO areas; the country in red |
| `country/<country>analysis_species_by_area.png` | Catch of the main species, split by fishing area, with the share of each area in the species' catch |
| `country/<country>analysis_area_total_production.png` | Total catch and share by fishing area |
| `country/<country>yearly_area_production.png` | Catch in each area over time |
| `country/<country>yearly_area_production_wrap.png` | One panel per area |
| `tables/<country>analysis_country_ranked_table.csv` | Average catch per decade, catch in the last five years and share in the last year of each species |

It returns the data behind the charts:

```{r}
names(morocco_global)
show_table(morocco_global$country_species_area_total, n = 8, digits = 1)
```

| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| `country_species_ranked` | Catch of the selected species by year |
| `country_species_ranked_coefs_data` | Their breakpoints |
| `table` | The table saved in `tables/` |
| `country_species_area_total` | Catch of the selected species in each area, and the share of each area in the species' catch |
| `country_yearly_area_production` | Catch in each area by year, and its share of the country's catch that year |

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `country_name` | FAO country name, as in the data | |
| `rank_range` | Ranks of the species shown, by the country's total catch over all years | `c(1, 10)` |
| `plot` | Save the charts | `TRUE` |
| `table` | Save the table in `tables/` | `TRUE` |
| `timeseries_analysis` | `TRUE`: species panel chart with linear trend and breakpoints; `FALSE`: with a smooth curve | `TRUE` |
| `time_analysis_text_displacement` | Position of the share labels in the panel chart: number of years after the first year with catch | `10` |
| `h_value` | Minimum length of a period between breakpoints: a fraction of the series or a number of years | `0.15` |
| `ZH` | Older way of asking for Chinese: `TRUE` is `lang = "zh"` | `FALSE` |
| `fill_scale` | Palette of the fishing area map, any choice of `map_palette` in `fao_settings()` | `NULL`: `map_palette` of `fao_settings()` |
| `lang` | Language of the chart text and names: `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | `NULL`: `"zh"` if `ZH = TRUE`, else the language of `fao_settings()` |
| `data_version` | FAO release: `"latest"`, `"bundled"` or a release such as `"2026.1.0"` (see [💾 FAO data](data.html)) | `"latest"` |
| `pptx` | Also save the charts as editable PowerPoint files | `FALSE`, or `pptx` of `fao_settings()` |

The breakpoints are found as described in [🌊 Fishing area analysis](fishing-areas.html)
(`strucchange::breakpoints()` with a constant mean in each period).

::: callout-tip
Country names follow FAO: e.g. `"Korea, Republic of"`, `"Russian Federation"`,
`"Taiwan Province of China"`. Find them with
`grep("Korea", unique(load_fao_data()$Country..Name.), value = TRUE)`.
:::
